statement: Assume Theorem 6.1, and let fϵ → f locally uniformly on D along the sequence of finite systems under consideration. Fix a bounded measurable base patch Q of positive measure with compact closure in R × I, a radius R ≥ 1, an error η > 0, an exceptional proportion 0 < τ < 1, and a maximum block length h∗ > 0. There exist 0 < h < h∗, G ⊂ Q, |Q \ G| ≤ τ|Q|, and a compact neighborhood K0 ⊂ D containing all Π(q) + hξ with q ∈ Q, ξ ∈ K ∩ BR, such that the following holds. If ∥fϵ − f∥L∞(K0) ≤ ηh/4, (6.19) then, simultaneously for every q ∈ G and every ξ ∈ K ∩ BR, |fϵ(Π(q) + hξ) − fϵ(Π(q)) − hA(q) · ξ| ≤ ηh. (6.20) In particular, for every finite family of such displacements, every information increment between two of them differs from its affine value by at most 2ηh. An alternating sum of r profile values whose affine contributions cancel has absolute value at most rηh. All dependencies have the order f, Q, R, η, τ, h∗ −→ h, G, K0 −→ ϵ0. For every member of the converging finite sequence with ϵ < ϵ0, (6.19) holds. If finitely many entropy identities also incur a total normalized ambiguity error at most B/ log(1/ϵ), one may, after choosing h, require in addition log(1/ϵ) ≥ B/(ηh). Each such combined identity then has at most one additional ηh of error. More generally one may prescribe any sequences ηℓ, τℓ ↓ 0 and h∗,ℓ ↓ 0 and select successively hℓ < h∗,ℓ, then the inner approximation thresholds. If P ℓ τℓ < ∞, almost every point of Q belongs to all but finitely many of the resulting Gℓ.
